title: Navigating Oceans with Magic Sunstones
hook: Vikings sailed open oceans without compasses using glowing calcite crystals.

scenes.text: Centuries before magnetic compasses reached Europe, Viking longships crossed the freezing, fog-shrouded North Atlantic all the way to America.

scenes.text: Medieval sagas speak of the legendary 'Sólarsteinn'—the mythical Sunstone said to reveal the hidden sun behind overcast skies.
scenes.imagePrompt: A transparent rhomboid Iceland spar calcite crystal resting on a weathered wooden chart table catching a glint of light. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Medieval sagas speak of the legendary 'Sólarsteinn'—the mythical Sunstone said to reveal the hidden sun behind overcast skies.

scenes.text: Modern scientists discovered this stone was Iceland spar: a birefringent calcite crystal that polarizes ultraviolet light.
scenes.imagePrompt: Scientific demonstration showing light splitting into two polarized beams through a clear crystal onto parchment paper. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Modern scientists discovered this stone was Iceland spar: a birefringent calcite crystal that polarizes ultraviolet light.

scenes.text: By rotating the crystal until both split light beams matched in brightness, navigators pinpointed the sun's exact heading within one degree.
